verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 7.4 'Without JavaScript' (no [D] mark): 'A Playwright run with JavaScript disabled checks, for every lesson, that the text, every default figure and every table are present.' SPEC 3 M9 figure table: beat 3 'T13 shadows on A2 with the flip and no black node', beat 6 'T13 restricted board on E6 with black nodes 2, 3, 4, 5'. SPEC 4 T13 (phase 6): 'Shadows: for real rank 1 and 2 a picture', 'Restricted board: drawn in Bourbaki order'. These passages support the finding's expected for M9.
verdicts.evidence: Read at f07eec6 (worktree detached there, clean; nothing built or run). (1) nojs.spec.ts:75-180, toolReport: the figure is boards[0] ?? drawings[0] ?? imgs[0]. A board is any visible [data-board-group] with a [data-node] beside an svg with children, so a T13 root passes as 'board' through its decoration. A drawing is any role=img element with childElementCount > 0 and a name, so empty <g> children are enough. blankParts reads only data-out=orbit-graph and [data-format][data-rows][data-cols], which are T12's parts (RT-FIX-P5-t12-a11y, DECISIONS.md:3406). No line reads data-out=shadow-picture or restricted-board. (2) M9.spec.ts:275-344, 'M9 renders without JavaScript': per instance it checks the decoration svg, the decoration and game-board buttons, colours, black-nodes, tau, the selected tab and the decoration table. For b7 it checks only restricted-name text. Beat 3's picture checks (M9.spec.ts:503-517, data-point and data-mult) run after hydrate(page, 'b3'), with JavaScript on. So without JavaScript nothing checks that b3's picture or b7's restricted nodes are present at all. (3) P6-A3 'the panels and the history' (DECISIONS.md ~3970): 'Only the open panel is rendered; a preset opens its panel at build time'. So the shadows and restricted panels are the configured default figures of those beats. (4) The reproducer, read as text at worktree-agent-ab01232faaf6b3607, asserts exactly the claim. (5) Records: RT-FIX-P3-test-integrity (DECISIONS.md:2583), RT-FIX-P4-tool-t10 (:3050) and RT-FIX-P5-t12-a11y (:3406) are builder records of the predicate. None is a [D], a section 10 default or an owner answer, and none covers T13 panels or the marks of a role=img drawing. P6-A4 'the tool root of an Atlas page is its opening figure' (:4002) chooses the root and does not set a predicate. The MERGE entries on P6-A3, P6-A4 and P6-size say nothing on this. The known-and-decided list has nothing on it. (6) Precedent: P5-RT-06-01, the same cause on T12, was not refuted (round-p5 out/RT-06-refute.json). gate-G6.md (report commit d59af4a, which names f07eec6 as the gate commit) records no open item on the no-JS figure check. No earlier phase 6 red-team round exists. Partial overstatement: the T14 half is on /atlas/B3/ and /tools/atlas/, which are not lessons. 7.4's sentence says 'for every lesson'. M10 has no tool root, so no lesson holds a T14 figure. The T13 half on M9 carries the cause on its own.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 failed because no sentence permits a no-JS run that skips a lesson's default figure, and 7.4 asks for every default figure on every lesson, with M9's table making the shadow picture (beat 3) and the restricted board (beat 6) figures. R2 holds only for the T14 half, since Atlas pages and the picker are not lessons, and the M9 half carries the cause. R3 failed because T13, T14 and M9 are phase 6 at gate G6. R4 does not apply, since no oracle quantity is involved. R5 failed because 7.4 and T13 carry no [D], and the predicate entries in DECISIONS.md are builder records that do not cover T13 or drawing marks. R6 failed because the P5-RT-06-01 fix and its regression test cover T12 only, gate-G6.md has no open item, and no earlier P6 round exists. Minor fits ('a test that could be stronger without being wrong'): the server markup does hold the figures today.

verdicts.citation: R6: build-plan/reports/orchestrator/round-p6/out/RT-03.json, finding P6-RT-03-02 ('restrictedBoard of E7 and E8 does not survive the worker wire'), confirmed in this round: out/RT-03-reproduce.json reproduced true, out/RT-03-refute.json refuted false, TALLY.md 'RT-03 verdicts: ... 02 CONFIRMED minor'. TALLY.md also lists P6-RT-06-02 as 'DUPLICATE of P6-RT-03-02 (same cause, the wire's specOf)'. RED-TEAM-COMMON 5: 'One cause, one finding. If two findings share a cause, merge them.' Supporting R1: CONTRACTS.md 4 'Board as its BoardSpec (rebuilt with resolveBoard)', with BoardSpec = string | { cartan; xy? } (no labels). The wire format is logged at DECISIONS.md:455 (P1-A2: 'a board { "$board": BoardSpec } (its name, or { cartan } ...)'), and its consequence for phase 6 restricted boards is recorded at DECISIONS.md:2247 (MERGE, phase 4, 'Passed to the owner and later phases').
verdicts.evidence: Same cause, same location, same observed values. P6-RT-03-02's location is 'site/src/lib/workerWire.ts serialize (a Board becomes { $board: specOf(board) }) and deserialize ($board rebuilt with resolveBoard)'. Its claim includes 'A named restricted board whose matrix is in orbit order comes back as the standard board of that name'. Its observed gives, for e8(-24), main-thread labels [4,3,2,1] with Cartan [[2,-1,0,0],[-1,2,-2,0],[0,-1,2,-1],[0,0,-1,2]], and through the wire labels [1,2,3,4] with [[2,-1,0,0],[-1,2,-1,0],[0,-2,2,-1],[0,0,-1,2]]. These are exactly P6-RT-06-02's values. Its proposedFix also covers this case ('Serialize a Board in a result with its matrix and labels, and its name, whenever it is not the standard board of its name'). The RT-03 reproducer reproduced the e8(-24) values in two runs. At f07eec6, workerWire.ts:58-61 reads 'export function specOf(board) { return board.name !== undefined ? board.name : { cartan: cartanNumbers(board) }; }' and serialize sends { $board: specOf(value) }, as both findings say. Supporting records: SPEC 6.6 makes a type name ('E8') denote the standard board, and BoardSpec carries no labels, so the contract's round trip cannot keep a restricted board's labels [4,3,2,1] under either spec form. P1-A2 logged 'its name, or { cartan }'. MERGE phase 4 recorded that a restricted board of phase 6 'would be rebuilt in the worker with its positions permuted'. MERGE on P6-A1 (DECISIONS.md:3520) names e8(-24) among the 7 named restricted boards whose matrix stays in orbit order. t13/model.ts:387 says rb.board is never read ('the worker rebuilds it by name'). SPEC 5.1 E-9 item 3 says only that restrictedBoard for E7 and E8 runs 'in a Web Worker behind a promise'. Note on R6's wording: RT-VERIFY 5.3 names gate-G6.md or an earlier round's merge report as the record. Here the record is the same round's confirmed finding, which the harness pointed to and the tally marks as a duplicate. Dropping this finding loses nothing, because the fixer of P6-RT-03-02 receives the same cause and case.
verdicts.reason: R6: the cause (workerWire.ts specOf sends a named board by its name, so resolveBoard rebuilds e8(-24)'s restricted board as the standard F4) is already reported and confirmed in this round as P6-RT-03-02, with the same location, case and values, and one cause gets one finding (RED-TEAM-COMMON 5). The relabelling is also the round trip that CONTRACTS 4 prescribes for a Board, logged by P1-A2 and passed to the owner by MERGE in phase 4 (R1, supporting).
